title: JRE 2271 - John Reeves
guestBio: John Reeves is an Alaskan gold miner who first came to public prominence on the 2012 National Geographic docu-series "Goldfathers." More recently, his ongoing search for gold uncovered the remains of thousands of Ice Age animals lying beneath the permafrost on his property. The discovery is featured in the 2019 documentary "Boneyard Alaska" and popular Instagram account @theboneyardalaska.
tldr: John Reeves is an Alaskan gold miner who discovered thousands of Ice Age animal remains frozen beneath his property

recap:
Joe sits down with John Reeves, an Alaskan gold miner who stumbled onto one of the most remarkable paleontological discoveries in recent memory. While running his gold mining operation in Alaska, Reeves and his team started pulling massive quantities of Ice Age animal bones out of the frozen ground. We're talking mammoth tusks, bison skeletons, and thousands of other specimens from animals that roamed Alaska during the Pleistocene era, all preserved in permafrost that's been frozen for tens of thousands of years.

The conversation dives deep into how Reeves initially discovered these bones while excavating for gold. What started as an odd curiosity became a full-blown operation documenting and cataloging the remains. Reeves talks about the sheer volume of bones coming out of the ground and how the thawing permafrost is exposing these deposits at an accelerating rate. The scientific implications are massive, and Reeves has become something of an unexpected expert in ice age fauna.

Joe and Reeves explore the mechanics of permafrost and why these animals remained so well preserved. The conversation touches on climate change and how warming temperatures are rapidly exposing fossils that have been locked away for millennia. Reeves explains the practical side of his operation, the challenges of mining in Alaska's extreme conditions, and how he's balanced his gold mining business with the responsibility of preserving these paleontological discoveries.

The episode features Reeves' genuine enthusiasm for both the gold and the bones, giving listeners insight into a unique intersection of commercial mining and scientific discovery. His Instagram account the Boneyard Alaska showcases the incredible finds, and the documentary work has brought attention to the area's paleontological significance. It's a fascinating look at how sometimes the most important discoveries come from unexpected places.
